raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #39173.

With `SGLANG_RAGGED_VERIFY_MODE=compact`, DSpark target verify can pack unequal numbers of tokens per request. A compact CUDA graph tier can also hold more requests than full verify windows: for example, 42 tokens over 8 slots captures as `[6, 6, 5, 5, 5, 5, 5, 5]`. Two DeepSeek-V4.1 components still assume `draft_token_num` tokens per request:

- `EngramHasher.forward` asserts `num_tokens == bs * draft_token_num`. Capture fails with `engram target-verify expects one equal block per request, got 42 tokens for 8 requests of 6`.
- `token_req_indices` calls `repeat_interleave(req, draft_token_num, output_size=num_tokens)`, which fails, or maps tokens to the wrong request, once the layout is not uniform.

As a result, DeepSeek-V4.1 compact verify fails on these layouts.

#40567 by @lidekang160122 identified both call sites and fixes them as part of a larger PD change. This PR fixes only the crash. It derives the token-to-request mapping in one shared helper and reuses Engram's existing extend kernel path, so it needs no kernel changes.

Depends on the shared-layout fix from #42709, now in main: both components read the verify layout inside the CUDA graph, and without it the DeepSeek-V4.1 graph variants captured first for a token tier would read a layout that replay does not refresh.

## Modifications

- `ragged_verify.py`: add `ragged_verify_token_rows(layout, num_tokens)`. It is a fixed-size `searchsorted` over the layout's `qo_indptr`, so it is safe under CUDA graph capture. Empty rows own no tokens, and the graph-padding tail maps to row `bs`.
- `EngramHasher.forward`: with a ragged layout, target verify uses the existing `MODE_EXTEND` path with `row = ragged_verify_token_rows(layout, num_tokens).clamp_max(bs - 1)` and `starts = layout.qo_indptr_device[:-1]`. As before, verify commits no history. Graph-padding tokens are hashed with the row the staged layout assigns them (a padding row, or the last row for the tail) and then discarded.
- `token_req_indices`: with a ragged layout, each token gets its request's pool index. The tail past the last request gets pool slot 0, like the padded rows of a dense verify graph; padding the staged layout assigns to a row gets that row's slot.
- Without a layout (static verify), both functions take the existing dense path unchanged.
- No change to capture slot sizing. The current `min(num_tokens, max_bs)` slots are valid once these components accept unequal rows.

## Accuracy Tests

- `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/dsv4/test_dsv41_compact_verify.py` (CPU tests and a CUDA graph replay test; all pass on an RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell):
  - Packed Engram hashes equal the hashes of each request verified alone on the dense path. Cases: the 42-token / 8-slot capture geometry, a batch with empty rows and a graph-padding tail, and one request in a 3-token graph. All three cases run with maximum n-gram sizes 4 and 8 and include a short prefix; the first two also include an image token. Engram history is unchanged.
  - A uniform layout gives the same Engram hashes and request indices as the dense path.
  - `token_req_indices` maps empty rows and the padding tail correctly.
  - A CUDA graph captured once is replayed with three different layouts, and Engram hashes on real tokens and request indices on all tokens match eager.
- `TestCapturedVariantsReadStagedLayout` (CPU, same file) calls `DecodeCudaGraphRunner`'s layout-capture helper twice for a 12-token tier, as the two DeepSeek-V4.1 attention variants do, stages live lengths [6, 1] for request slots 7 and 9, and checks that `token_req_indices` and `EngramHasher` read the live boundaries from either variant's layout. Without the shared layout from #42709, the first variant maps the real tokens to [7, 7, 9, 9, 0, 0, 0]. All six tests in the file, including the CUDA graph replay test, pass on an RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell.
- `test/registered/spec/dspark/test_ragged_verify.py`: unit test of `ragged_verify_token_rows`.
- An ad-hoc comparison with #40567's implementation on an RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120), not part of this PR, gave bit-identical Engram hashes on real tokens and bit-identical request indices on all tokens. Coverage was 146 eager layouts (73 at each of n-gram sizes 4 and 8) and 22 CUDA graph replays, including the 42-token geometry, single-request graphs of 1 to 5 tokens, empty rows, and padding tails.
- End to end, I served DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with #40567's implementation and #42709 (not with this exact diff). Setup: 4x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120, PCIe), TP4/EP2, DSpark gamma=5, compact verify with a profiled SPS table. I compared target log-probs of generated tokens with a plain prefill of the same text. The maximum per-token difference was 0.79-0.86 nats, the same as static verify. A temperature-1 run of 32 streams had no repetition loops.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The change itself adds one `searchsorted` per Engram call and per low-ratio request lookup in compact verify. Static verify is unchanged. Not benchmarked separately.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

+"""DeepSeek-V4.1 per-token request lookups under compact (packed) target verify."""
+
+import unittest
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import torch
+from torch import nn
+
+from sglang.srt.environ import envs
+from sglang.srt.layers.attention.dsv4.dsv41_sparse import token_req_indices
+from sglang.srt.layers.engram import EngramHasher
+from sglang.srt.model_executor.forward_batch_info import ForwardMode
+from sglang.srt.speculative.ragged_verify import RaggedVerifyLayout
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci, register_cuda_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=5, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=20, stage="base-b-kernel-unit", runner_config="1-gpu-large")
+
+WIDTH = 6  # gamma + 1
+IMAGE_TOKEN = 127
+DEVICES = ["cpu", "cuda"] if torch.cuda.is_available() else ["cpu"]
+
+
+def make_hasher(device, n=4, num_slots=16):
+    h = EngramHasher.__new__(EngramHasher)
+    nn.Module.__init__(h)
+    h.max_ngram_size = n
+    h.pad_id = 0
+    h.image_token_id = IMAGE_TOKEN
+    g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(n)
+    h.register_buffer("token_map", ((torch.arange(128) * 7) % 128).to(device))
+    h.register_buffer("multipliers", torch.randint(1, 1 << 20, (2, n), generator=g))
+    h.register_buffer("primes", torch.randint(1000, 5000, (2, n - 1, 2), generator=g))
+    h.register_buffer("offsets", torch.arange((n - 1) * 2).expand(2, -1) * 5000)
+    h.to(device)
+    h.init_history(num_slots, device)
+    h.history.copy_(torch.randint(1, 127, h.history.shape, generator=g))
+    return h
+
+
+def verify_batch(slots, positions, layout, draft_token_num=WIDTH):
+    return SimpleNamespace(
+        forward_mode=ForwardMode.TARGET_VERIFY,
+        req_pool_indices=slots,
+        positions=positions,
+        spec_info=SimpleNamespace(
+            draft_token_num=draft_token_num, ragged_verify_layout=layout
+        ),
+        out_cache_loc=None if positions is None else torch.ones_like(positions),
+    )
+
+
+def packed_layout(lens, num_tokens, device):
+    return RaggedVerifyLayout.from_verify_lens_device(
+        verify_lens=torch.tensor(lens, dtype=torch.int32, device=device),
+        graph_num_tokens=num_tokens,
+    )
+
+
+def packed_inputs(lens, num_tokens, device, seed=0):
+    g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)
+    total = sum(lens)
+    ids = torch.randint(0, IMAGE_TOKEN, (num_tokens,), generator=g)
+    if total > 3:
+        ids[total // 2] = IMAGE_TOKEN  # an image token blocks the lookback
+    starts = torch.randint(0, 40, (len(lens),), generator=g)
+    starts[0] = 1  # a short prefix blocks the older shifts
+    positions = torch.zeros(num_tokens, dtype=torch.int64)
+    positions[:total] = torch.cat(
+        [torch.arange(n) + s for n, s in zip(lens, starts.tolist())]
+    )
+    return ids.to(device), positions.to(device)
+
+
+class TestEngramCompactVerify(CustomTestCase):
+    def check_against_dense(self, h, lens, num_tokens, device):
+        slots = torch.arange(len(lens), device=device) * 2 + 1
+        ids, positions = packed_inputs(lens, num_tokens, device)
+        history = h.history.clone()
+        layout = packed_layout(lens, num_tokens, device)
+        out = h(ids, verify_batch(slots, positions, layout))
+        self.assertEqual(out.shape[0], num_tokens)
+        start = 0
+        for i, n in enumerate(lens):
+            if n == 0:
+                continue
+            # Oracle: the request verified alone on the dense path.
+            run = slice(start, start + n)
+            dense = h(
+                ids[run],
+                verify_batch(slots[i : i + 1], positions[run], None, draft_token_num=n),
+            )
+            torch.testing.assert_close(out[run], dense, rtol=0, atol=0)
+            start += n
+        torch.testing.assert_close(h.history, history, rtol=0, atol=0)
+
+    def test_matches_per_request_dense_verify(self):
+        for device in DEVICES:
+            for n in (4, 8):
+                h = make_hasher(device, n)
+                with self.subTest(device=device, n=n):
+                    # Capture geometry from #39173: 42 tokens over 8 slots.
+                    self.check_against_dense(h, [6, 6, 5, 5, 5, 5, 5, 5], 42, device)
+                    # Empty rows and a graph-padding tail.
+                    self.check_against_dense(h, [3, 0, 6, 1, 0, 2], 18, device)
+                    # One request in a 3-token graph.
+                    self.check_against_dense(h, [3, 0, 0], 3, device)
+
+    def test_uniform_layout_matches_dense_path(self):
+        for device in DEVICES:
+            h = make_hasher(device)
+            slots = torch.tensor([3, 1, 4], device=device)
+            ids, positions = packed_inputs([WIDTH] * 3, 3 * WIDTH, device)
+            layout = packed_layout([WIDTH] * 3, 3 * WIDTH, device)
+            torch.testing.assert_close(
+                h(ids, verify_batch(slots, positions, layout)),
+                h(ids, verify_batch(slots, positions, None)),
+                rtol=0,
+                atol=0,
+            )
+
+    @unittest.skipUnless(torch.cuda.is_available(), "requires CUDA")
+    def test_cuda_graph_replay_follows_layout(self):
+        h = make_hasher("cuda", 8)
+        num_tokens, num_slots = 12, 8
+        slots = torch.arange(num_slots, device="cuda") + 2
+        ids = torch.zeros(num_tokens, dtype=torch.int64, device="cuda")
+        positions = torch.zeros(num_tokens, dtype=torch.int64, device="cuda")
+        layout = packed_layout([2, 2, 2, 2, 1, 1, 1, 1], num_tokens, "cuda")
+        batch = verify_batch(slots, positions, layout)
+        stream = torch.cuda.Stream()
+        stream.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())
+        with torch.cuda.stream(stream):
+            h(ids, batch), token_req_indices(batch, num_tokens=num_tokens)
+        torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_stream(stream)
+        graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+        with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+            out = h(ids, batch)
+            req = token_req_indices(batch, num_tokens=num_tokens)
+        for seed, lens in enumerate(
+            ([6, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0], [1] * 8, [0, 3, 0, 2, 0, 0, 1, 0])
+        ):
